data.name: Jesse
data.gender_notes: Jesse is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Jesse means 'God's gift'. In the Bible, Jesse was a king of the tribe of Judah and the father of King David. The name Jesse carries the meaning “God's gift” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Jesse usually hope their child will grow to embody god's gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Jesse belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jesse total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_english.name: Jesse

data.cultural_impact: The name Jesse holds great significance in Judeo-Christian culture due to its biblical origins. In the Old Testament book of Samuel, Jesse is depicted as a shepherd king of the tribe of Judah. He is described as a mighty man of valor, and he is also the father of King David, who is considered one of the greatest kings in Jewish and Christian history.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Jesse carries a profound spiritual meaning, highlighting the idea that all of us are God's gifts to the world. In the biblical narrative, Jesse is chosen by God to be the father of King David, who is anointed as the future king of Israel. This suggests that even the most seemingly insignificant individuals can be used by God to accomplish great things.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jesse represents humility and strength, rooted in the unwavering faith of the ancient Jewish king. His name, derived from the Hebrew word 'ish' meaning 'poor' or 'humble', signifies a deep connection to the divine, reminding us to remain grounded in our spiritual journey.

biblical_reference.note: Jesse is mentioned as the father of David in the biblical account

historical_references.reference: The Old Testament prophecy in Isaiah 11:1 refers to a future king of Israel whose lineage is traced back to Jesse, the father of King David. This prophecy was believed to have been written around the 8th century BC.
The New Testament names Jesus as the descendant of Jesse, as recorded in Matthew 1:6 and Luke 3:32. Jesus' genealogy is traced back to Abraham, then to Jesse, and ultimately to King David.
